ui.scope: Authored local scenarios. No real cluster, network, scheduler or controller is run. Repairs affect only this lesson.
ui.evidence: Inspect the listed evidence before applying a repair.
ui.fixed: The local repair has been applied. Inspect the resulting state before continuing.
ui.observe: Inspect the resulting Pod or endpoints in Properties.
ui.evidenceError: Some required evidence has not been inspected. Open the listed object views first.
ui.diagnosisError: The selected explanation does not match the observations. Recheck the evidence.
ui.complete: Both independent cases are complete: evidence inspected, diagnosis justified, repair applied and result checked.
ui.noEvents: No events in this authored snapshot.
ui.noLogs: No container logs are available in this snapshot. The container may not have started.
ui.noSecrets: Secret values are never included. Only reference names and key names are shown.
ui.memory: Progress lasts while this library is open. Closing it clears lesson state.
ui.observations: Given scenario observations · not Kubernetes API fields
ui.support: Which observations distinguish your diagnosis from the alternatives?

diagnoses.selector: The Service selector does not match the application Pod labels.
diagnoses.port: The Service forwards to a different port from the application listener.
diagnoses.readiness: The readiness probe checks a path that the application does not serve.
diagnoses.startup: Liveness restarts the container before slow initialization can finish.
diagnoses.image: The requested image tag is absent from the supplied image catalogue.
diagnoses.command: The application exits because its arguments are invalid.
diagnoses.environment: The environment value was captured before the ConfigMap changed.
diagnoses.secret: The required Secret key name does not exist.
diagnoses.requests: The CPU request does not fit the remaining request budget.
diagnoses.memory: The container exceeded its memory limit; the recorded reason is OOMKilled.
diagnoses.credentials: The image registry requires different credentials.
diagnoses.usage: Low observed CPU usage means any CPU request will fit.
diagnoses.replicas: More replicas alone will repair this configuration.

selector.goal: Restore traffic without changing the application. Compare Service, Pod and EndpointSlice.
selector.hint: Compare spec.selector with metadata.labels; an empty ready endpoint set needs an explanation.
selector.why: Matching the intended Pod labels supplies backends; a Service does not create Pods.
selector.supportWhy: Readiness and a correct port do not show that the selector matches. Compare the Service selector with the intended Pod labels.

port.goal: Restore traffic when ready backends already exist. Check both Service ports and the listener.
port.hint: A ready address alone is not enough: compare targetPort with the application port.
port.why: targetPort is the backend port. A ready endpoint does not prove end-to-end reachability.
port.supportWhy: Matching labels and a ready address do not show that the ports match. Compare targetPort with the application listener.

readiness.goal: Make a running application ready for Service traffic without adding restarts.
readiness.hint: Compare the readiness HTTP path with logs. The live endpoint and readiness endpoint serve different checks.
readiness.why: Readiness controls normal Service eligibility; a failed readiness check alone does not restart a container.
readiness.supportWhy: Running and a working liveness endpoint do not establish readiness. Compare the readiness path with the observed HTTP results.

startup.goal: Allow the documented slow initialization while retaining liveness protection.
startup.hint: Compare initialization time with the probe window. A startup probe delays liveness and readiness until it succeeds.
startup.why: The authored startup budget covers the observed cold start. It is not a universal probe configuration.
startup.supportWhy: An image name and a running phase do not explain initialization restarts. Compare the liveness window with the documented cold start.

image.goal: Start the application using an image present in the supplied catalogue.
image.hint: Read the pull failure reason and the approved tag. Do not invent logs for a container that never started.
image.why: A missing manifest is addressed by the reviewed image reference, not by repeatedly pulling the same missing tag.
image.supportWhy: Pending and zero restarts do not identify a missing tag. Compare the requested image with the approved reference and the pull event.

command.goal: Find why a pulled image still exits and fix the application launch arguments.
command.hint: Compare previous-container logs with the workload arguments. CrashLoopBackOff is a symptom, not a root cause.
command.why: The observed exit was caused by an invalid option. Restarting unchanged arguments would repeat that failure.
command.supportWhy: A successful pull and a restart count do not establish an argument error. Compare the actual args with the previous-container log.

environment.goal: Use the current ConfigMap value in the application environment. Compare the reference and the running snapshot.
environment.hint: lesson-revision is an arbitrary annotation name, not a Kubernetes restart command. Changing it under spec.template changes the Deployment Pod template and triggers a rollout. Changing only Deployment metadata outside the template does not. New Pods get new UIDs; containers read ConfigMap environment values when they are created. A running process keeps its old environment. Inspect the template change, the new Pod UID and MODE after the repair. Mounted files and application reloads are different mechanisms.
environment.why: lesson-revision is an arbitrary annotation name, not a Kubernetes restart command. Changing it under spec.template changes the Deployment Pod template and triggers a rollout. Changing only Deployment metadata outside the template does not. New Pods get new UIDs; containers read ConfigMap environment values when they are created. A running process keeps its old environment. Inspect the template change, the new Pod UID and MODE after the repair. Mounted files and application reloads are different mechanisms.
environment.supportWhy: A running phase and a Pod identity do not prove stale environment. Compare the current ConfigMap, captured MODE and update timing.

secret.goal: Resolve the required Secret reference without reading or inventing a Secret value.
secret.hint: Compare secretKeyRef.key with the listed key names and the startup event. Making the reference optional does not supply the required value.
secret.why: The corrected reference uses an existing key. Key names do not reveal the Secret value or prove that access is authorized.
secret.supportWhy: Opaque and a Pod identity do not show which key is absent. Compare secretKeyRef.key with the available key names and event.

requests.goal: Schedule the workload using its supplied validated CPU request, without overcommitting the request budget.
requests.hint: Compare allocatable minus already allocated requests with this request. Current CPU use is not that budget.
requests.why: The validated request fits the given remaining budget. A higher CPU limit alone cannot make an oversized request schedulable.
requests.supportWhy: Usage and CPU limits do not establish scheduler fit. Compare the request, remaining request budget and validated application request.

memory.goal: Resolve the recorded OOMKilled condition within the supplied approved memory budget.
memory.hint: Compare the recorded termination reason, workload limit, validated working set and remaining node budget.
memory.why: The scoped limit change accommodates the documented working set. Exit code alone would not prove OOMKilled; memory requirements are workload-specific.
memory.supportWhy: A healthy Node and a running phase do not explain the previous termination. Compare OOMKilled, the memory limit and the supplied working set.

checks.network: Requests to the application fail. Find the cause from the supplied observations and restore traffic.
checks.probes: The application is not reliably available. Diagnose the supplied observations and restore availability.
checks.runtime: The workload does not reach stable operation. Diagnose the supplied observations and repair it.
checks.config: The application is not operating with its required configuration. Find and repair the cause.
checks.resources: The workload is not operating reliably. Find a repair justified by the supplied observations and application requirements.

probes.title: How the three probes differ
probes.readiness: Readiness asks whether the container can accept traffic. Failure makes the Pod ineligible for ordinary Service traffic without itself restarting the container.
probes.liveness: Liveness detects an unhealthy container. Repeated failures can restart that container; a running process alone does not prove readiness.
probes.startup: Startup protects slow initialization: liveness and readiness wait for its success. With periodSeconds=5 and failureThreshold=12 the approximate budget is 60 seconds. Compare it with the documented cold start; these are not universal settings.

rollout.title: Why a template annotation replaces Pods
rollout.change: lesson-revision is an arbitrary annotation name, not a Kubernetes restart command. Changing it under spec.template changes the Deployment Pod template and triggers a rollout. Changing only Deployment metadata outside the template does not.
rollout.environment: New Pods get new UIDs; containers read ConfigMap environment values when they are created. A running process keeps its old environment. Inspect the template change, the new Pod UID and MODE after the repair. Mounted files and application reloads are different mechanisms.

repairFeedback.replicas: More replicas copy the same configuration. They do not correct the mismatched field.
repairFeedback.sameSelector: The selector already matches the Pod. Reapplying it leaves the wrong targetPort unchanged.
repairFeedback.samePort: targetPort already matches the listener. Reapplying it leaves the selector mismatch unchanged.
repairFeedback.liveness: The /wrong path returns 404. Setting liveness to it does not fix readiness and can restart a healthy container.
repairFeedback.readiness: Readiness does not suspend liveness. The container can still be restarted before initialization finishes.
repairFeedback.threshold: Reducing failureThreshold to 1 shortens the liveness window and makes the early restart more likely.
repairFeedback.pullPolicy: Always pulls the same image reference again. It cannot create a missing tag or correct application arguments.
repairFeedback.credentials: The pull event says manifest unknown, not unauthorized. Registry credentials do not create the missing tag.
repairFeedback.sameConfig: The ConfigMap already has that value. Writing it again does not change the running process environment.
repairFeedback.containerPort: containerPort does not reload environment variables or create a new application process.
repairFeedback.optional: Making the reference optional leaves the required value absent; it does not fix the key name.
repairFeedback.cpuLimit: A CPU limit does not reduce the scheduler request. The oversized request still does not fit.
repairFeedback.increaseCPU: Increasing the request consumes more of the remaining budget. Compare it with the validated application request.
repairFeedback.memoryCPU: A CPU limit does not increase the memory limit that caused the recorded OOMKilled.
repairFeedback.reduceMemory: Reducing the memory limit below the documented working set makes the memory shortage worse.
repairFeedback.secretCredentials: imagePullSecrets configures image-registry authentication. It does not fix secretKeyRef.key for the application environment.
repairFeedback.pullArguments: The image was already pulled. Pulling it again does not correct the unsupported argument recorded in the previous-container log.
